And this is the record we believe on, so that we can go on to perfection, having escaped the corruption of the world; that it be well with us. That we may trust His commandments for our benefit, and be an example and a blessing to others, adding to His testimony. Drawing others to Christ.

teachings.title: Waiting on God's perfect timing
teachings.summary: Impatient waiting in trials should give way to remembering God's bountiful dealing and salvation, since patience in waiting on the Lord renews strength and builds godliness.
teachings.text:
Psalm 13 beautifully captures a very real feeling of the Christian life, the impatient waiting for God's perfect timing, turning into an acknowledgement that He has dealt bountifully with us.

It can be easy to slip into despair when facing trials. It can be easy for us as humans, weak in the flesh, to see the enemy seemingly triumph. To pray and wait upon the Lord, but feel like He may have forgotten you in regards to your trouble.

We've discussed the idea that even as martyred saints in Heaven, this impatient call for the Lord to hurry and fulfill His judgment, occurs. How much more can this take hold in our finite flesh?

As Peter reminds us;

**2 Peter 3:8–9**
*But, beloved, be not ignorant of this one thing, that one day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day. The Lord is not slack concerning his promise, as some men count slackness; but is longsuffering to us-ward, not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance*.

God calls upon His faithful to wait. And in that waiting, there is promise as well.

**Isaiah 40:31**
*But they that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint.*

In our patience, God gives us added strength. It is part of a ladder of virtue in the Christian life, elevating us to godliness.

**2 Peter 1:5–8**
*And beside this, giving all diligence, add to your faith virtue; and to virtue knowledge; And to knowledge temperance; and to temperance patience; and to patience godliness; And to godliness brotherly kindness; and to brotherly kindness charity. For if these things be in you, and abound, they make you that ye shall neither be barren nor unfruitful in the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.*

In the end, our prayers for God to act, and reminders that He has promised to tend to our welfare, and bring us peace from our enemies must inevitably lead to our recognition of His mercies and blessings. Of His salvation.

Because, as we call out to Him, it is impossible to not remember the very reason we are trusting in Him, beginning with eternal life granted through Jesus. And with the heavenly perspective of God's grace, it is incredibly difficult to continue in complaint. *Because he hath dealt bountifully with* us. We've already received more than we could ever deserve.

teachings.title: Forsake all and gain an hundredfold
teachings.summary: The more we are willing to lose family, comfort and nation for Christ, the more God blesses, so we should let go and trust Him rather than fear or politics.
teachings.text:
One of the hardest things to understand in faith is that the more we care about the things of God, despising even the flesh we have, our family, our comfort, and living for Jesus, the more we are blessed, the better things are in our lives and those we love.

It's a paradox that many can't get around, but for those who do, you see how it works.

When Jesus says "*Suppose ye that I am come to give peace on earth? I tell you, Nay; but rather division: For from henceforth there shall be five in one house divided, three against two, and two against three. The father shall be divided against the son, and the son against the father; the mother against the daughter, and the daughter against the mother; the mother in law against her daughter in law, and the daughter in law against her mother in law,*" (**Luke 12**) he isn't saying you have to hate them, but rather be prepared to lose them. To be willing that you lose them all to gain Christ. To understand that many will reject Him and you, and die perishing. Many will hate you for it. But we aren't to be troubled.

Because as Jesus also says, "*And every one that hath forsaken houses, or brethren, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or lands, for my name's sake, shall receive an hundredfold, and shall inherit everlasting life.(Matthew 19)”*

Like Job, who having lost everything in this world but his life, yet he loved the Lord, and received it all back in abundance, so to if we are willing to lose everything, on faith, we will gain what we lost and more.

If you have unbelieving children or parents you love, this can be difficult to get past. But if you're willing to let go and trust God, even if you may lose them, you will be surprised at how many come around.

This goes for comfort, nation, work...all the cares of life. The more you are willing to suffer and yet trust Him, the more you will gain.

If you're afraid of the future and desperate to see some kind of assurance, or place your faith in whatever reactions you think you should take, politics you get involved with, fed posting and red pilling, you will lose it all. But trust in Christ, despising those things for the Lord's sake, and you will gain so much more.

I have seen it. I have been so blessed. Let go. Have faith.

teachings.title: Be careful for nothing
teachings.summary: The believer's normal state should be rejoicing and prayer with thanksgiving instead of worry, content in any state and trusting God to supply all need.
teachings.text:
Paul ends what is one of the most beautifully written thank you notes of all time. Full of exhortation and doctrine, blessings and thanks. Lessons for how to live for God and be at peace in Christ.

*Rejoice in the Lord always: and I say again rejoice.Let your moderation be known unto all men. The Lord is at hand. Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God. And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.*

This should be the default state of your Christian life. Joy, not worrying and fearful for the cares of this world but trusting, in prayer and supplication to the Lord, in thanksgiving for the blessings and the tribulation by which the Spirit strengthens us. Having the peace with God that comes from being Christ's.

If your walk isn't this, if troubles of the world weigh you down to bitterness, anger, resentment, envy and strife, then know it doesn't have to be this way. Walk less in the flesh and more in the spirit. In daily prayer, scripture reading, singing songs of praise and the psalms. Knowing with confidence your blessed assurance, that *God shall supply all your need according to his riches in glory by Christ Jesus.*

Think upon things of virtue, honesty, pure, true. Meditate on the law of God, and you will learn to praise Him and be content with whatever state you find yourself in. Abased or abounding. Satisfied with what you have, thankful to God that you have it. Knowing for certain in faith that you can do all things through Christ which strengthens us. Living faith to faith.

And be fruitful, not as the world measures in wealth and status, but in souls won by your faithful service to God, reached by His word, a path lit by the light of your example.

teachings.title: Letting go of fear for this world
teachings.summary: Fear and worldly cares brought him misery, and accepting by faith that they do not matter, with thanks whatever the outcome, is where God blesses most.
teachings.text:
For me, in my journey here, it was fear and concerns of this world that led me consistently to misery, anger and resentment. The Bible warns us against this inclination of man, towards faith in all things. And in the paradox of the wisdom of God, it is accepting on faith that these things don't matter, where you will see the most change. That you're willing to count for loss but gain in Christ are the areas God will bless you the most abundantly.

Fear for family, work, relationships with others...all the trauma and drama of this world, all things work for good when you love God and trust Him, thankful regardless of outcome. Just have to let go.

The more you do, the more you stay in the word and do what your supposed to, without worry or fear or entitled expectations of what you "deserve" the more you will find you get what you need. And the more you bring people you love to the same peace, that passes all understanding, that comes from the grace God shows His children.

teachings.title: Let my people go worship
teachings.summary: God led with letting His people worship, so Christians must make sure any persecution they suffer is for Christ's name, not for being riotous or rendering evil for evil.
teachings.text:
Moses and Aaron go before the Pharaoh, and speak the words God had gave them; allow the Israelites a 3 day release from their labors that they may assemble to worship Him. (3 days without labor, works, just as we see during Christ's death, burial and resurrection). And as God said, Pharaoh's heart was hardened and he not only said no, but added to the people's labors, making them gather their own straw for brick, while keeping the same expectations for output. And the taskmasters over them tell the people that it is due to Moses and Aaron's plea that they be allowed free to go and worship God.

And the people turn to criticize Moses, who in turn goes before the Lord and asks why God has not instantly freed them, and instead made their situation worse.

As we have already seen, Moses is not the most stalwart man of faith, and the people, as we will continually see, are stiff-necked and impatient with the Lord.

But we are called to be faithful and long suffering. To understand that God's timing is perfect and ours is lacking. To take joy in being persecuted for His name.

This is an important factor that needs to be reinforced, especially today.

God didn't lead with freeing the nation of Israel from the Egyptians. He didn't begin with plagues and curses. He led with "let my people worship." From that point on, everything that happens to the Egyptians is due to their reaction to this plea. The persecution of His people will be for His name's sake. This has to be every Christians starting point. Regardless of how harshly we are treated, make it be for God's sake. For Jesus' name. Not because we are riotous. Not because we will render evil for evil. But because our oppressors despise the Lord.

teachings.title: A sweet savour of Christ
teachings.summary: We should not care how we look to the world, since to the perishing we are the savour of death, but our obedience is a sweet savour to God and all things work together for good.
teachings.text:
*And the officers of the children of Israel did see that they were in evil case, after it was said, Ye shall not minish ought from your bricks of your daily task. And they met Moses and Aaron, who stood in the way, as they came forth from Pharaoh: And they said unto them, The Lord look upon you, and judge; because ye have made our savour to be abhorred in the eyes of Pharaoh, and in the eyes of his servants, to put a sword in their hand to slay us.*

The elders of Israel, its failed human leaders, take to task Moses and Aaron who, having done what God told them to do, even saying what God told them to say.

Remember in **Exodus 4**:

*And Moses and Aaron went and gathered together all the elders of the children of Israel: And Aaron spake all the words which the Lord had spoken unto Moses, and did the signs in the sight of the people. And the people believed: and when they heard that the Lord had visited the children of Israel, and that he had looked upon their affliction, then they bowed their heads and worshipped.*

God had told Moses that Pharaoh would not allow them to go to worship Him. Moses told Aaron all of what God told him, and Aaron *spake all the words.*

They knew it wasn't going to be as easy. But at the first sign of tribulation, the elders come against Moses and Aaron for preaching and doing God's word. And they say "*you have made our savour abhorred in the eyes of Pharaoh."* These leaders are more concerned with how they look to the world than to God. But look what Paul writes in **2 Corinthians 2:15-17**:

*For we are unto God a sweet savour of Christ, in them that are saved, and in them that perish: To the one we are the savour of death unto death; and to the other the savour of life unto life. And who is sufficient for these things? For we are not as many, which corrupt the word of God: but as of sincerity, but as of God, in the sight of God speak we in Christ.*

To the world, we stink like death, because we remind them that they are perishing, but our obedience to God in Christ is a sweet savour unto the Lord.

We shouldn't worry about what the world thinks of us, even if it means persecution. We need to remember that all things, not some things, not a few things, not only good things, but *ALL* things work together for good to them that love God.

teachings.title: Faith Over Fear in Great Tribulation
teachings.summary: Facing the beast's war on the saints, believers must trust God rather than their own preparations, love the brethren, and look to Him to provide in the wilderness.
teachings.text:
The moment many were waiting for, the prophecy of the beast, the antichrist and his false prophet. The mark and the number. 666.

The serpent, that old dragon Satan, gives power to the beast, who is mighty and given power to make war on the saints for 3.5 years. 42 months. He is described as having a head wound, and yet lives. A counterfeit Christ. Dead yet risen.

And as he makes war on the saints, those who fight with sword will die by sword, and those who bring others to captivity will be made captive. The beast, the antichrist will have the Uno reverse card and play it often. Testing the patience of the saints. Our faith in Jesus to save us out of Great Tribulation.

This is a hard saying. The Bible tells us again and again that we who keep watch, knowing the signs, staying in the word, won't be taken unawares. But we are expected to lean entirely on the Lord for our salvation from the beast. Not of ourselves.

Just like spiritual salvation. *And they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb, and by the word of their testimony; and they loved not their lives unto the death.*

We are to trust God, and not love our own lives, even if it means death of the body. *But he that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved.*

*And to wait for his Son from heaven, whom he raised from the dead, even Jesus, which delivered us from the wrath to come.*

We may die for the cause of Christ and for having His testimony. We may be cut off from buying and selling for refusing the mark of the beast, during a time we are told there will be great famines and pestilences. And all our preparing and stockpiling won't save us. But faith can.

And in that faith, in time of tribulation, whether the normal troubles that we face today, or that Great Tribulation to come, we are to love our brethren in the faith. Caring for one another. Sharing what we have with other saints.

*But as touching brotherly love ye need not that I write unto you: for ye yourselves are taught of God to love one another. And indeed ye do it toward all the brethren... but we beseech you, brethren, that ye increase more and more; And that ye study to be quiet, and to do your own business, and to work with your own hands, as we commanded you; That ye may walk honestly toward them that are without, and that ye may have lack of nothing.*

Having faith that there is a place provided us by God, that we may be nourished...

*And to the woman were given two wings of a great eagle, that she might fly into the wilderness, into her place, where she is nourished for a time, and times, and half a time, from the face of the serpent.*

It's easy to fall into fear at the prospect of being persecuted for our belief. At being cut off by famine and refusing to worship the beast. At being taken unawares and ill prepared. At facing death and starvation. At being cast out into the wilderness.

But there in the wilderness is where God provides. Manna from heaven. Quails in abundance. Locusts and wild honey. Fed by ravens. Water from flint. It takes but faith. The patience He demands of His people.

Faith over fear.

teachings.title: In Every Thing Give Thanks
teachings.summary: Giving thanks in all things, good or bad, and trusting God's will will change a believer's life more than anything short of salvation.
teachings.text:
And so, a simple exercise for those of us seeking to grow in faith and understanding, by trusting in God's word and obeying His will as revealed by the same word;

**1 Thessalonians 5:18**
*In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you*

Are you thankful in all things? Do you know how to be abased, and how to abound? To trust that you can do all things through Christ, who strengthens you?

Do you have faith to **know** *that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose?*

Are you thankful for all things, good or bad, that the will of the Father for you in Christ Jesus is kept, and in so doing, regardless of what it is, good or bad, you give thanks?

This one exercise of being thankful to the Lord and trusting His will regardless of our own will, having faith that by seeking Him and following His will for us we will be blessed and rewarded, even if it isn't something we can see as yet... Even if it remains hope on His promise...This one thing will change your life as profoundly as anything short of salvation. I testify to it, God is my witness. He is not slack concerning His promises. His will be done. In all things give thanks.

teachings.title: Climbing out of the hole sin dug
teachings.summary: Being saved does not remove every consequence of past sin; God gives the rope and light to climb out, and chastens those who despise it and backslide.
teachings.text:
A lot of new Christians, and many not-so-new, will become frustrated and despair that when they got saved, and began "turning their life around," that they still had to endure the pain and hard work of getting up out of the hole their old man had dug for them with their sin.

But that hole was a grave. And in it was death. And God has given us the rope to climb out of it, and the light above to guide us from the darkness.

That while the worst consequences are mitigated, and miraculous opportunities to escape are granted them, there is still a process of shedding sin in their life. There is still lost opportunity and easier paths lost to them by their choices. There's still a price to pay in this world.

People sometimes can only see the walls of the hole they are in, and the light above seems small and distant. And the climb difficult, to where they take occasion to despise the rope they've been given. And they backslide.

Sometimes God shakes the rope to draw their attention and get them back focused on the light.

As we will see with the children of Israel, that sometimes we see falling back into sin, going back to servitude in Egypt, as easier than getting right with God. And God will remind us the foolishness of this. Harshly.

*My son, despise not the chastening of the Lord; neither be weary of his correction: For whom the Lord loveth he correcteth; even as a father the son in whom he delighteth*

teachings.title: God will repay those who persecute His saints
teachings.summary: God promises vengeance on all who persecute His children, so believers are not doormats but rest in His deliverance and are not ashamed of the gospel.
teachings.text:
And so, knowing all this, what then? What further hope have we than eternity? Laying up treasure in Heaven? Giving glory to God in our tribulation that more may benefit? What else could we possibly need?

God. In His grace and love promises us one more thing; Vengeance. He will repay. And all who have wronged Him, who have persecuted His sons and daughters, will repay. For He is a consuming fire.

We aren't simply "Christ-cucks" acting as punching bags. We aren't floor mats to be trampled on. We have the Spirit inside us, we have blessing upon blessing given us. We see God move in our lives in mighty ways, when we walk after the spirit, and we have felt the reproach of God, who scourges every son, when we walk after the flesh.

The natural man receiveth not the things of God for they are spiritually discerned.

They can't understand this. The worldly men are full of fear and without hope because they don't believe, and not having faith, they cannot see.

**1 Corinthians 1:25-29**
*Because the foolishness of God is wiser than men; and the weakness of God is stronger than men. For ye see your calling, brethren, how that not many wise men after the flesh, not many mighty, not many noble, are called: But God hath chosen the foolish things of the world to confound the wise; and God hath chosen the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty; And base things of the world, and things which are despised, hath God chosen, yea, and things which are not, to bring to nought things that are: That no flesh should glory in his presence.*

Don't be ashamed of the Gospel, for it is the power of God unto salvation and in it we will never be ashamed. God will always deliver.

teachings.title: Aaron's grief and God's longsuffering
teachings.summary: God is merciful and patient when grief leaves our heart unable to do His will that day, as long as we do not curse God or backslide.
teachings.text:
After having kin remove the remains, Moses calls Eleazar and Ithamar, Aaron's remaining sons, and instructs them to do as the Lord commanded, to eat the sin offering, cooked by the same fire that killed their brothers, that came from the Lord. To eat it beside the altar, because this is a holy thing, designed to teach the congregation of the separation of holy from unholy. From clean and unclean.

But later, Moses sees their portion of the offering burnt without the camp. Likely in fear of divine retribution, Moses seeks out the sons to rebuke them, but Aaron says it was his own fault. That he couldn't bear to do it given the events of the day and the loss of his eldest two sons. Aaron admits the error, but appeals to the fact that it wouldn't have been done in the spirit of God's command had he gone along and ate it, and that it wouldn't have been acceptable given his state. This excuse is acceptable to Moses.

It is important to make this distinction, that while we must obey God's commands and seek to diligently follow what His word tells us is right, there are times where our heart isn't in it. Our spirit is low. And unlike those who seek to add their own works to the glory of God, kindling His wrath, the Lord is understanding of our own weakness and longsuffering in His mercy.

Aaron held his peace. He had accepted the judgment of God. But he was still grieved. He was on God's program but it was too bitter that day. Aaron resumed his duties following this, but it was too much to bear at the time.

God is merciful and loves us. He is understanding that sometimes the truth of His word is bitter to us, in the flesh. His judgments may seem harsh to us at the time, and we may need a little time to come to acceptance. We must not use that occasion to curse God or to backslide. But He is patient.

teachings.title: Alms, prayer and fasting in secret, and take no thought
teachings.summary: Jesus condemns public religious show, vain repetitions and treasure on earth, which he likens to the Catholic church, and teaches us to seek God's kingdom first and not worry, since worry is worship of the god of this world.
teachings.text:
The sermon of Jesus Christ on the mount continues. I rather think this is representative of Jesus preaching during His earthly ministry, and many themes here are repeated in the other Gospels to showcase and teach us His perfect and flawless doctrine.

Give alms in secret to men, for our Father will reward you. Pray in secret, not making a show of it, and the Father who knows all our needs before we do will openly reward you. Don't pray as the heathen do, with vain repetitions thinking they will be heard for much speaking. Don't place your heart on treasures in this world, material wealth, but rather treasure what you may lay up in Heaven. Don't make a public show of fasting and doing without. Don't even let anyone know that you are fasting.

Essentially, don't act like the Catholic Church.

Jesus says that they who pray and give alms in public to fanfare, who fast, abstaining from meats, giving up treats, to be seen as holy to men, those who pray with novenas and roseries, repeating the same words again and again, a vain prayer of repetition, those who place their treasure on earth, serving mammon, materialists with gilded shrines and golden fixtures, ornate buildings full of idols...all these get their reward, Christ assures us. And it isn't a blessing but a curse.

No man can serve two masters, as scripture says. You can't serve an earthly, fleshly, material god of this world, and serve the Father. *He will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other.*

And so Jesus tells us that worry for materialism, for vain glory, for grudges held, debt unforgiven, the accumulation of things, this is serving Mammon. Not God. Not seeking the Kingdom of Heaven. Eyes full of darkness.

Worry is a prayer to the god of this world. Fear is the worship of him.

But we are children of the light and are looking forward to a better country, establishing the works thereof. Storing up the crowns and precious stones of heavenly rewards. Keeping our eyes turned to Heaven.

Taking no thought for what we wear, shelter, food. Trusting God to provide for our needs as He does for His creation throughout nature. Living faith to faith. Unafraid.

*Seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.*

*Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof.*

Don't worry about tomorrow, if the Lord blesses us with a tomorrow, He will provide. The evil of today is sufficient enough without adding cares for things yet to come. But keep in faith. He will provide.

teachings.title: Vengeance is His: the day of His wrath
teachings.summary: The disobedient will meet Christ's coming in fear and everlasting destruction, and believers suffering tribulation can take heart that vengeance belongs to God and He is faithful.
teachings.text:
As for those who are disobedient to the Gospel, this day is met with fear.

**Revelation 6:15-17**
*And the kings of the earth, and the great men, and the rich men, and the chief captains, and the mighty men, and every bondman, and every free man, hid themselves in the dens and in the rocks of the mountains; And said to the mountains and rocks, Fall on us, and hide us from the face of him that sitteth on the throne, and from the wrath of the Lamb: For the great day of his wrath is come; and who shall be able to stand?*

Or as Paul writes in **2 Thessalonians 2:9** they *shall be punished with everlasting destruction from the presence of the Lord, and from the glory of his power.*

The martyrs in Heaven, especially those killed in the Great Tribulation, cry out for vengeance and the firey judgment of God. God's promise is that they will receive fire and damnation for their wickedness, and all shall know His power.

God is longsuffering, and His timing may frustrate us as man, as He does not count the time as we do, "a thousand years as a day," the way Peter describes, but His promise is true, and He is faithful to those of us who have faith in His Son.

Vengeance is His. Take heart in that, though the world may hate us, though we may know tribulation, we, like the Thessalonicans can take heart.

**Matthew 16:27** *For the Son of man shall come in the glory of his Father with his angels; and then he shall reward every man according to his works.*

teachings.title: Therefore being justified by faith
teachings.summary: Justified by faith we have peace with God now and stand in grace, and even glory in tribulations that work patience, experience and hope.
teachings.text:
Therefore.

When we see this word we have to ask ourselves "what's it there for?" What does it refer back to?

Well, 4 chapters of Paul logically and with irrefutable proof from scripture that all are under sin and need salvation, and that salvation is through faith in Jesus Christ, by the grace of God.

Therefore. Therefore what?

*Being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ.*

As the heavenly hosts proclaimed in the hills of Bethlehem at the birth of the man Christ Jesus;

*Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will toward men.*

The peace and goodwill on earth was come from God to man. Not the peace of men not warring. Not goodwill between tribes. But the enmity of wrath in the transgressions of man made justified by the peace offering of His only begotten Son.

We are justified by faith alone. There is nothing more noted. We have already concluded that by the works of the law no man shall be justified. We already know that by faith, Abraham became father to all who believe. We already know that the judgment of God is upon Jew and Greek alike. And that Jesus as propitiation for our sin has given us salvation from the wrath we deserve.

*Therefore being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ.*

What's more; By faith we have access into the grace wherein we stand, and rejoice in hope of the glory of God.

Believing, we are given grace, and by grace, God is given the glory for our salvation. Note, "wherein we stand." This isn't the future, this isn't a process. This is now, at the time of our repentance towards belief in Christ as our redeemer we then, at that moment, stand in grace. And rejoice.

And we not only rejoice in the glory of God's grace that provides us with salvation through faith, because it shows the mercy and judgment and righteousness of God (which remember is one way His glory is revealed to man from Heaven), we also glory in tribulations here on earth, knowing they are a refining fire; that worketh patience, which brings experience, and experience brings hope. Hope builds faith.

*Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen*.

Hope is the sure knowledge that a thing will be that is not yet. The object of faith. Tribulation in our lives, not only persecution for our faith, but just general troubles like health, finance, whatever things common to all men, saved or unsaved, all of it gives opportunity to glorify the Lord, as it makes our faith sharper as we are brought out of it by His mercy and blessings, better for having experienced it.

And our hope is fufifiled in the love of God, by the comforter, the Holy Ghost, which is given us, who indwells with us, quickening our spirit and leading us to that peace which passes all understanding, even in turmoil and crisis.

Our faith in man, traditions, our own works, all will leave us ashamed at some point. But the hope we have in Christ Jesus will never bring us shame. God never lets us down.

teachings.title: Render to Caesar what is Caesar's
teachings.summary: God uses the persecution of believers to convert even rulers, so paying taxes and suffering wrong is a trifle next to eternal treasure.
teachings.text:
And this is a pattern we see, God using the persecution of believers, even of Christ, to give the increase. God uses the weak things of this world to confound the strong. And in doing so, they are often converted.

Nebuchadnezzar believed, and repented of the evil He would do. Kings came around to free all Judah from captivity.

Publicans, centurions, even some Pharisees, all men with power and authority came to believe, and in doing so were given the same spirit we are. To be good ministers, to rightly judge.

Paul, despite his being able to be released when arrested in Jerusalem, rather went to Rome in chains that he may minister the Gospel to the house of Caesar.

This world isn't ours and the things of it are at best wood, hay and stubble, but the treasure we seek is of Heaven and incorruptible. Things of eternal value.

And when we look at the eternal, this mortal life is given perspective. And rendering to Caesar what is Caesar's is a trifling thing. Paying custom and tribute; taxes, is nothing. God provided us what we have and will again. Even from the mouth of a fish.

And if we are defrauded, Jesus says to not only let it go, but offer more. They take your coat, give them your cloak also. If they force you to walk a mile, go two. If they strike you, give them your other cheek that they may see what they are doing for what it is, and make the decision in your defiance to either strike again, or in shame back down. And perhaps by your chaste conversation be converted. By your stripes they may be healed.

teachings.title: Win souls, don't hide in a bunker
teachings.summary: Christians in the collapsing West should not panic or flee to the hills but, like Jeremiah in Jerusalem, stay in their communities winning souls.
teachings.text:
By the way, this is what every Christian who is in the collapsing West should take to heart. Instead of spiraling in fear and reactionary panic, We should remember the promises of God. That we will be delivered. While we may suffer tribulation even unto death, we shall be delivered.

*And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.*

Jeremiah is facing the assured and imminent destruction of his people. Witnessing a famine overtake the land from drought. He is vexed by the filthy conversation of the wicked everyday. And yet he remains separated unto God. He continues to call others to believe, by the word of God.

Yes, Jeremiah is calling out evil. And yes, he's warning the people that they should turn from their sins. But more importantly he's calling people to be saved by faith. He's winning souls.

As depraved and wicked as America is, and knowing the wrath that is upon our people, that has already begun, being ruled by women and foreigners which is a punishment on nations. Having escalating violence against us as a people. Seeing sexual immorality and degeneracy become normalized and targeting children. As wicked as all of that is, we are still a light unto the world as a righteous remnant of believing Christians. There is no other bastion of believers as large in the world. We are blessed with the freedom to preach the gospel to every creature and the resources to actually get it done.

*The harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few; Pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he will send forth labourers into his harvest.*

Instead of prepping for doomsday and hiding our light under a bushel in some mountainous retreat, We should be winning souls. Jeremiah isn't in the wilderness far away from the people, but in Jerusalem, the heart of darkness.

Now, I believe it's important to secure the safety of your family, because as a man that's our job, and knowing how to care for them if SHTF is vital, what's more important is doing the work of the Lord. If the great tribulation came tomorrow ( and it's not, we've got a ways down to go), but if the great tribulation came tomorrow, we wouldn't be heading to the hills eating freeze-dried. MREs, but going into the heart of our community, trying to win souls before the day of judgment.

This is a great encouragement. God has given us something tangible that we can do. And we can join in with other members of our community to ensure our deliverance spiritually even if physically it's too late. And in doing so we might delay that judgment and secure a future for our children.

The world is always going to be going to hell in a hand basket. But we are in the time of the harvest and so we should head out to bring in the sheaves.

teachings.title: Seek the Lord and He gives rest
teachings.summary: God promises to reward those who diligently seek Him and will answer prayers asked according to His will, in His time and as we need, so we simply have to trust Him.
teachings.text:
*Because we have sought the Lord our God, we have sought him, and he hath given us rest on every side.*

This is a promise of God. Something worthy to place our faith in.

**Hebrews 11:6**
*But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him.*

**Matthew 7:7-8**
*Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you: For every one that asketh receiveth; and he that seeketh findeth; and to him that knocketh it shall be opened.*

**1 John 5:14-15**
*And this is the confidence that we have in him, that, if we ask any thing according to his will, he heareth us: And if we know that he hear us, whatsoever we ask, we know that we have the petitions that we desired of him.*

It will be in His time. It may not look like what you imagined. It may be what you need not what you want. But He will answer our prayers, and deliver us with His mighty hand from whatever troubles us. We simply have to trust Him. Amen

teachings.title: Building the wall while the mockers scoff
teachings.summary: Like Nehemiah's builders, believers growing in sanctification will be mocked even by family, and must keep building, put on the whole armour of God, and pray for one another.
teachings.text:
And so as the construction continued, and the mockers increased their scorn and ridicule, it became apparent to the scorners, like Sanballat, a governor in Samaria, Tobiah the Ammonite, that the Jews were serious in the endeavor.

The wall wasn't finished but it was getting there.

In our Christian life, we may experience initial scoffing by our friends, family and neighbors. People who doubt our conversion because they know us. The old man. And those things they say may throw us off our course. Make us doubt ourselves.

When Tobiah says a fox could topple their wall, it's like when a brother or parent scoffs at our faith and our attempts to get right. But we see from Nehemiah how to handle this. To turn their reproach upon their own head. To trust in the Lord.

Their mocking comes not only at our expense, but it reveals in themselves to their own sin and iniquity.

**Proverbs 29:27**
*An unjust man is an abomination to the just: and he that is upright in the way is abomination to the wicked.*

Jesus says He came into this world to divide it. Even family.

**John 3:19-21**
*And this is the condemnation, that light is come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil. For every one that doeth evil hateth the light, neither cometh to the light, lest his deeds should be reproved. But he that doeth truth cometh to the light, that his deeds may be made manifest, that they are wrought in God.*

So the scoffers in Nehemiah's day set their minds to violence in an effort to stop the construction. This also can be how some people will react to your sanctification, as you build upon the foundation Christ has laid in your heart. So we must stand watch, and continue building. We put on the whole armor of God.

**Ephesians 6:10-18**
*Finally, my brethren, be strong in the Lord, and in the power of his might. Put on the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil. For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places. Wherefore take unto you the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to withstand in the evil day, and having done all, to stand. Stand therefore, having your loins girt about with truth, and having on the breastplate of righteousness; And your feet shod with the preparation of the gospel of peace; Above all, taking the shield of faith, wherewith ye shall be able to quench all the fiery darts of the wicked. And take the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God: Praying always with all prayer and supplication in the Spirit, and watching thereunto with all perseverance and supplication for all saints*

The prayers of the saints are our spears, always at the ready. Pray for one another to stand strong to the mocking. Our brothers and sisters in Christ. Knowing we have each other's back, as the people of Jerusalem did against the mockers.

teachings.title: Seek His face in prayer
teachings.summary: As David modeled, believers are commanded to seek God's face in faith and prayer, confessing sin and trusting His faithfulness and deliverance through trouble.
teachings.text:
Continuing Psalm 27, after establishing the faith on which he stands, and the confidence he has on the promises of God, David as psalmist cries out to the Lord for His mercy, to hear his prayer.

As these are meant to be sung or said, as model prayers or devotional worship, we are called to do the same. To call upon the mercy of the Lord. To bless His longsuffering and grace towards us, and petition the Lord with prayer.

**Hebrews 11:6**
*But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him.*

When we seek the Lord, it is obedience to His command to seek His face. To search for Him. As individuals and as a nation of believers.

**2 Chronicles 7:14**
*If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.*

*Seek and ye shall find*, the Bible says. Our God is merciful to hear our prayers and to reward those that in faith, have sought Him out. What a humbling and amazing thing to be considered worthy of attention by our Creator.

David continues, meekly asking for forgiveness if there are any transgressions that may have displeased the Lord. Asking for His favor, to not forsake us in times of trouble, yet having the understanding that our trouble may be due to our own unresolved sin. Either way, *O God of* our *salvation,* hear our prayers.

In the very next breath, David affirms the steadfast faithfulness of the Lord, that even if our own parents forsake us, He remains true.

Expressing fear and doubt while recognizing the truth of the promises of God is a human thing, and we see this play out on our own minds, even as it does David's. We are a weak and needy people, and we need God involved in every aspect of our lives.

Remember this, and be open to His teaching. Be open to hearing His voice in scripture, recognizing the chastening in our life, seeing His mercy towards us, and wrath revealed from Heaven, and fearing Him, always.

He shows us the path. He gives us a way out of every temptation.

**1 Corinthians 10:13**
*There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man: but God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it.*

We may ask for His help to see the deliverance He has for us, even as our adversaries seek to destroy us with their lies and schemes.

*I had fainted, unless I had believed to see the goodness of the LORD in the land of the living.*

The evidence of God's grace and mercy to His people gives us faith and strength to carry on. This is a key reason why it is important to praise Him in the congregation, to edify those going through the trials of life, to have hope. That all things work together for good. To wait, patiently for the Lord to move. To be of good courage, knowing what He as done for others and has done for us in the past. Knowing our present suffering leads to the glory we are partakers in, through Christ.

**Romans 8:35–37**
*Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? shall tribulation, or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or peril, or sword? As it is written, For thy sake we are killed all the day long; we are accounted as sheep for the slaughter. Nay, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him that loved us.*

Amen
